impugned order  [2024:RJ-JD:22130] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-5493/2 2.
It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused- petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4.

I have considered the submissions made by the parties and perused the case diary as well as the material available on record more particularly the statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. on 25.03.2024 and 28.03.2024 respectively.
5. A plain reading of the statements of victim recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. making it clear that she was in relation with the petitioner.
She wanted to marry with him but her parents were not agreeable and, therefore, on 19.03.2024, she left the company of her parents and joined the association of the petitioner at Ashok Udhyan.
Whereafter they took a train to go to Agra, Uttar Pradesh, where they lived in a house of one relative of petitioner.
She, in an unambiguous term, has stated that no force was used by the petitioner; rather, she was willing to establish physical relationship with him.
Thus, there remains no question that she was not a consenting party.

[2024:RJ-JD:22130] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-5493/2024]
6. As far as the question of age of the victim is concerned, at this stage, the submission raised on behalf of the petitioner regarding sanctity of the document cannot be ignored and of course it would be the subject of the trial as to whether the victim was definitely a girl below the age of 18 years at that relevant point of time.
7. At this stage, when the petitioner has been sent to the judicial custody and there is high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude, this Court feels that further incarceration of the petitioner is not warranted.
In light of these facts and circumstances, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.

8. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates Rakesh Singh vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:22130) on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192428471/
2 of hearing as and when called upon to do so.
